en: That champion was a mighty wrestler,
He was a giant whose head would not fit,
He was exceedingly cunning and fierce,
His imposing presence seemed enough to frighten you,
He looked as though he would spare no life,
A calamity to anyone who challenged his strength,
Among the Kyrgyz his appearance was fiercely towering,
He seemed as fierce as an eagle,
His spirit returned again as he descended,
Wondering what sort of man it was,
When Joloy opened his eyes and looked,
He suddenly twisted his thick neck,
He had withered [?] like a soul,
Snorting through his nose,
His disordered coat would not close,
His moustaches curling,
Brandishing his battle-axe,
His might was concentrated in his neck,
Dust obscured his sight,
His wretched horse stood blinking,
When he noticed the one roaring,
He stood startled without moving,
An enemy roared beside you,
An enemy roared beside you,
His pursuer was drawing near,
He shut it, letting no one inside,
The stricken beast began to advance,
As they confronted each other, it became a conflagration,
The black multitude itself opposed him,
The arrow in his hand,
Enemies of every kind,
Each of them lashed with whips,
Setting out straight against the countless host,
When hardship descended upon them,
Ak Zholtoy watched what was happening,
He stood watching from the gray youth,
He had seen the people of Bukhara,
He did not let the contest continue,
He had the ready pacer galloped,
He fought with those who had taken lives,
Ebegei and Kogoy, the two lions,
Having heard all manner of things from the people,
They lived by making solemn pledges,
Seeking scraps from plunder—
They made their living by this,
Ebegei and Kogoy themselves went,
Their still-living eyes,
What had been prepared before their eyes,
There was a moment to start a quarrel,
He could move forward, taking heart,
Kogoy himself went to help,
Ebegei gathered a force,
There was a time when his skirts froze,
Seeking the trail of the boar,
The two men descended into the cool,
Seeing the dark sight here,
To the tiger-like hero Seitek,
To the warrior Ak Zholtoy,
The familiar Kongur became enraged,
There came a time when he stared at his foe,
His dark eyes filled with tears,
It was a sound like a sharp report,
The enemy came and seized him,
Wagging his tongue as though coated with salt,
When he saw him shouting,
Then he sent out a summons from Koydon,
He tied up the sheep droppings,
His insides boiled like syrup,
He drove on the surging reed-like host,
A malformed, venomous slave,
Panting, they became ninety,
His quarrelsome appearance was frightening,
Each man, seeing his enemy,
They broke apart when the time of disorder came,
The reason they had fallen into disorder,
Not one could step forward,
All turned about, unable to look,
Unable to master what was within them all,
Not acting with a single purpose,
Their manner of moving was aflame,
Not submitting to where they were driven,
They made the empty land seem like a settlement,
As though they stood crushed and exhausted,
Saying what, did he strike this one?
He did not carry away this one's fury.
This did not come from his pure heart
Struck down with no shepherd
A soul who drove away and sharpened his spirit
The bloodied sword, Kozoy’s blade
Fighting the infidel in patterned ranks
From the turmoil of worldly life
From the battle in that place
That soul bowed and broke
Now wandering and lying there
What fault had the people committed
Saying he was an ignorant man
Does his beast-like soul not know
His charger was broken down
If there is thought in the event
When the true world departed, it stirred
Do they still not understand life
If the spoken rumor is true
The arriving noble will appear
That ruined man was without a sword
Does he not seek justice from the khan
If he is a soul without an age
On Judgment Day upon the narrow road
If the warrior’s law is true
Will he not mount beneath the black-edged sword
Starting strife where there was no enemy
Will he lead them to the mountain ridge
A Chinese soul without guilt
Human protection scarcely between the two
Will he not create a hell
These two men, Ebedey and Kozoy
Will one cut bear the guilt
Without making blood-feud from battle
If he sobs in one place
The red steel would be girded
The world from the father
If he quarrels with God
Will he simply remain covered
Will the enemy draw near to us
God forbid those two men
They themselves were the raging ones
They were the eyes of two enemy hosts
Starting turmoil for an attack
It was the time they arrayed their ranks
I leave the wicked ones to God
Like horns against the enemy
No one entered the twisting trial
The wicked ones who stood divided
If one cuts them, there is no milk
Ebedey and Kozoy, two wicked men
Helplessly they made a quarrel
They broke the unity of the people
Across Talas, crooked and straight
Kongor struck with his strength
Ebedey and Kozoy became warriors
Who knows whose misfortune it was
Ebedey and Kozoy prevailed
The two sat in the saddle
He suffered at my side
Their faith was corrupted
That one soul from the faithful
Then not one soul was spared
Driving the white livestock through the mountains
Raising a loud battle cry
Again a warrior for this torment
He did not dismount from his horse
None truly ordered the liquor
There were no truths spoken by heroes
No man destroyed the beast
Making strife on a roadless way
There was no fool worse than this
Four descended and struck a thousand
Turning Kozoy’s face
Did Charak stand dividing them
These two men who never aged
Were they God-struck beasts
So spoke Ak Joltoy
Shaking his head at the dream’s meaning
He listened and turned
Unable to find the entrusted one
He came among the people
Giving counsel and reflecting
Your dear uncle Joltoy
Carried his weapons
There is worth in turning from the straight path
There is guilt upon the brow
There is a flowing black whip
What anger had spoken
O child, there is one who said drive him here
The eye cannot measure the wrestler
One who rejoiced and played
Drawing horses from many racers
If he comes, strike without holding back
He changed his good name
He arrayed the exhausted army
The age would be true if he lived
Your words truly remained for spring
Each of his words to every person
To a person with wisdom
If you hear it, reflect
Concerning your uncle Ak Joltoy
Ebedey and Kozoy were gone
The red-eyed one left for battle
He had a soul that struck with the sword
At his head was a dark companion
If a war host came directly
The heavens thundered and wailed
We will prepare much powder and shot
Whose eye a crow had pecked,
Who washed his back in cool water.
Taking a bullet from the hostile people,
Splitting stone with his beak,
Making the base of the walnut tree whistle,
From the wrestler whom no horse could charge,
Who gained renown by wrestling face-to-face,
Who went to the brown autumn pasture,
Whom the swift bird could not catch,
Who rose mightily above the clouds,
Who set birch twigs upon the water,
Whose green juniper covered the sky,
Training him amid the shouting,
The giant hogweed of the heavens,
Saying he had routed the Kazayka mounts,
Dear Zholtoy called out,
From Medeyzu [?],
He had his homeland sought this way,
From which place had he fled,
Light covered his pale eyes,
His collar was of patterned felt,
Found in Talas,
The fearless golden eagle,
Who had never seen a mature mare,
The swift horse, like a mullah in white bagdan,
When he encountered the golden eagle,
Not inferior to a mountain eagle,
Not yielding to a crag eagle,
The little pup brought down livestock.
Ak Zholtoy, riding bareback,
From atop Kulansur,
He sprang down like an arrow,
My knowing Zhadygoy,
When turmoil was put into his mouth,
Against all the others,
Fleeing into the hollow between them,
A crow had pecked out his eye,
Ak Zholtoy, without a sound,
Making the patches into horses,
Taking the blind enemy as his aim,
Voicing his abundant wisdom,
His white neck called Kökürök,
Whenever he began to speak,
Until the many came to know,
If they jabbed with spears,
As though thrusting straight at the face,
There, upon the open steppe,
There were campaigns of every kind,
Every cry of Ak Zholtoy,
Hurling himself like an arrow,
Hey, at Kozloy's [?] voice,
They drew their swords with a flourish,
The heroes brought them on and raced.
Hear your turn,
Calling you a tiger among them,
A strange snow gave birth—I am a Sart,
Erchiy and Kozhoy, the two friends,
So you were the elder sister who passed,
He went far away; let the deed be completed,
Like a shepherd extending a spear,
There is neither distant China nor Kyzyl,
Without turning back through the ages,
One who has not come since the time of the sword,
Think, my sweet heart,
